title: Design a Key-Value Store
summary: Design a distributed key-value store like DynamoDB or Redis Cluster.
body:
Design a distributed key-value store like DynamoDB or Redis Cluster.

## Scenario

Design a distributed key-value store that supports put(key, value) and get(key) operations with high availability.

## Requirements

- Automatic data partitioning across nodes
- Data replication for fault tolerance
- Consistency tuning (strong vs eventual)
- Automatic failure detection and recovery
- Support for 1M operations/second

## Constraints

- Each value up to 1MB
- Read latency p99 < 10ms
- No single point of failure
- Handle node additions/removals gracefully

## What a strong answer covers

- Consistent hashing for partitioning
- Replication strategy (quorum reads/writes)
- Conflict resolution (vector clocks vs LWW)
- Failure detection (gossip protocol)
- Merkle trees for anti-entropy

## Reference walkthrough

Consistent hashing with virtual nodes for even distribution. N=3 replicas with configurable W and R quorum. Vector clocks for conflict detection, application-level resolution. Gossip protocol for membership and failure detection. Merkle trees per partition for background sync. Hinted handoff for temporary failures.
